column3: §FILM_FACT sheets / model_yellow / model_src · open of the model-marked set · FILM_DXF2BIM_YELLOW_MARKINGS.md m01
column4: M: {sheets} drawings from our own export, opened in the Modeller.
column5: M: The Duplex sample, as {sheets} DXF drawings written by our own export, opened in the Modeller. | F: It already knows every sheet? | M: Plans, elevations, roof, section. {model_yellow} yellow rows. Every value says: from model.

column3: §FILM_FACT mark_lines / mark_z / mark_z_y · code card read from the FRONT sheet
column4: M: A marking is a short text inside the drawing.
column5: F: Where does it read that from? | M: From the drawing itself. A marking is a short text on its own layer, DXF2BIM-MARK: a key, an equals sign, a value. | F: That one sits on a line. | M: A level datum sits at the height it names: {mark_z} metres. Nothing is kept in a side file.

column3: §FILM_FACT by_counts · dxf2marks.js describe: no @BY = stated in the file
column4: M: The end of each text says who stated it.
column5: M: The end of each text says who stated it. By model: our export derived it from the model. By user: a person stated it. No ending: it was typed in the CAD file.

column3: §FILM_FACT plain_marks / open_blocking / open_yellow · open of the plain set
column4: M: The same drawings, markings removed. Blocked.
column5: M: Now the same drawings with every marking removed: what a CAD program hands you. | F: Blocked. | M: {open_blocking} items. No sheet has a role. And {open_yellow} rows are yellow.

column3: §FILM_FACT r1_rows / r1_rules / r1_sample · yellow list round 1
column4: M: Yellow: read from the drawing, not yours yet.
column5: F: What does yellow mean? | M: A value read from the drawing, with its source. Here the file header says millimetres. It is a suggestion: the field stays empty until you accept it.

column3: §FILM_FACT one_row / one_left / one_src / r1_after_yellow · confirm, then Accept all
column4: M: One tick: it is yours. Accept all takes the rest.
column5: M: Tick one row. That sheet's units now say: you. {one_left} rows left. | F: And the rest? | M: Accept all takes the lot. A row you ignore fills nothing.

column3: §FILM_FACT role_picks / role_why / r2_rows / r2_rules · role picks, round 2
column4: M: Choose each role. The list grows to {r2_rows} rows.
column5: M: These titles end in a scale, so the role is not read: choose it, {role_picks} times. | F: More yellow. | M: {r2_rows} rows: grid labels on their lines, level datums from the level texts, faces from the sheet names, and the section cut.

column3: §FILM_FACT cut_suggested / cut_title / cut_typed / r2_after_cut / cut_src · the cut typed over (usability P3)
column4: F: Is the cut right? | M: No. Type it from the title.
column5: F: Is every row right? | M: Not this one. The cut was read from two grid bubbles marked A. The section's title says X equals {cut_title}. | F: So I type it. | M: A typed value beats a suggestion. The row goes, and the field says: you.

column3: §FILM_FACT acceptall_below_px / r2_after · Accept all at the end of the list
column4: M: Read, then Accept all, at the end of the list.
column5: M: Then Accept all. It sits at the end of the list. | F: Without reading? | M: Read them. Accept all takes every row it shows.

column3: §FILM_FACT set_typed / r3_rows · set name once, PR-SET
column4: M: The set name: typed once, offered to the rest.
column5: M: The set name is not in the drawing. Type it once; the other {r3_rows} sheets get it as yellow. Accept.

column3: §FILM_FACT level_1 / level_2 / level_title / r4_rows · plan levels, PR-HAXIS
column4: M: Each plan's level, from its title.
column5: F: Which storey is which? | M: Each plan states its level: {level_1} and {level_2} metres, as the plan titles say. With the levels in, each elevation's horizontal axis is fitted to the plan grid: {r4_rows} more rows.

column3: §FILM_FACT roof_level / roof_top / roof_typed / after_roof_blocking · roof level and roof top (usability P5)
column4: M: The roof top, typed on {roof_typed} sheets.
column5: M: The roof plan's level, then the roof top, {roof_top} metres, from the level text. Typed on the roof plan, each elevation and the section: {roof_typed} times the same number today.

column3: §FILM_FACT front_marks / sheets_done_blocking · FRONT card + camera to the sheets in 3D
column4: M: Each sheet now knows where it stands.
column5: F: What does an elevation need? | M: Its face, its horizontal axis, its level datums, its grid labels. | F: And then? | M: Each sheet knows where it stands: plans at their level, elevations on their face, the section on its cut.

column3: §FILM_FACT verdict / item / item_cam · Verdict section + one item zoomed
column4: M: The verdict lists what is missing. It fills nothing.
column5: M: The sheets are complete. The verdict: {sheets_done_blocking} blocking items. Click one, and the drawing zooms to it. | F: Does it fill them in? | M: Never. It lists them.

column3: §FILM_FACT walltop_ticks / walltop_blocking · Wall tops
column4: M: One statement per plan: {walltop_blocking} left.
column5: M: Interior wall heights are in no elevation. One statement per plan: these walls run to the slab above. {walltop_blocking} items left.

column3: §FILM_FACT convert_status / doors_head · Convert refused
column4: M: Doors and windows: still listed. Convert says why not.
column5: F: And these? | M: Door heights and window products come from a schedule, not from the drawing. Until they are stated, Convert is refused, and says why.

column3: §FILM_FACT saved_n / saved_lines / saved_by · Save marked copies + code card of the saved section
column4: M: Save marked copies: every value now sits in its drawing.
column5: M: Save marked copies: {saved_n} DXF files. Every value you accepted or typed is now a marking inside its drawing. | F: By user? | M: By user. The opened files are unchanged.

column3: §FILM_FACT reopen_yellow / reopen_blocking / reopen_same · re-open the marked copies
column4: M: Open them again: nothing to choose.
column5: M: Open the marked copies in a fresh page. {reopen_yellow} yellow rows, nothing to choose again, and the same verdict: {reopen_blocking} items.

column3: §FILM_FACT limits · limits card
column4: F: What was not shown? | M: Listed on the card.
column5: F: What was not shown? | M: Doors, windows, layers, element defaults. And today: the suggested cut is wrong on our standard sets, titles with a scale are not read, the roof top is typed {roof_typed} times, and the list is long. Each has a proposal; none is built yet.

column3: credits card
column4: M: Markings: inside the drawing, yellow until yours.
column5: M: The markings: inside the drawing, yellow until they are yours.
